title: How many birds are at stake?
hook: Would your gift scale with a hundredfold change in the birds protected?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Compare scope-sensitive and scope-insensitive valuations without claiming every donor is insensitive.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Compare scope-sensitive and scope-insensitive valuations without claiming every donor is insensitive.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: An illustrative valuation is €80 to save 2,000 birds. What is that value per thousand birds? Toy inputs A=[2000, 80]; B=[200000, 88].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[40, 2000, 80], [0.44, 200000, 88]]. Labels: €/1000 birds, Birds, Total €.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The total valuation and the value per protected unit answer different questions. The two scopes have nearly similar totals but very different per-unit values. That pattern can be inspected without asserting that every person ignores scope.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Birds=200000, Stated value €=88. What is €/1000 birds? Answer: 0.44.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Birds=200000, Stated value €=88. What is €/1000 birds?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 0.44. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: People would pay about the same to save 2,000, 20,000 or 200,000 birds: $80, $78 and $88 (Desvousges et al., 1993).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Compare scope-sensitive and scope-insensitive valuations without claiming every donor is insensitive.
